title: Vela Origins private deploy — kickstart scratch diary
content:
Context: quick field notes after intro call w/ Vela Origins (CTO = R. Park, infra lead = S. Nwosu). Small biotech SaaS, strict PHI-adjacent data rules, wants private deploy in co-lo + optional air-gapped mode later. This is my personal scratchpad — messy.

Call summary (2025-11-03):
- Goal: replace current brittle LLM proxy (lambda-based) with a robust private deployment that meets p95 latency <= 60ms for short completions and sustained throughput ~40–60 rps per tenant.
- Must support both streaming chat API and embed generation for indexing.
- Data residency: everything must stay on their VPC/co-lo; logs allowed but only aggregated metrics (no raw prompts stored).
- Security: KMS/HSM required for model keys + customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) + optional YubiHSM on-prem.
- Compliance ask: audit log export to their SIEM (Splunk) and quarterly access review reports.
- Timeline: pilot targeting Jan 2026 (8 week runway for proof-of-concept), production by Q2 2026 depending on performance.

Rough technical constraints / requirements:
- Hardware: they have access to 4x A100 (80GB) hosts in co-lo; want guidance on whether to use as multi-instance or node pool. Prefer lower maintenance.
- Network: strict egress rules; any fallback to hosted models is blocked by policy unless routed through a customer-controlled proxy (unlikely).
- Model selection: will start with an open 70B variant (quantizable). They care about tokenization parity w/ SOTA; we should recommend a 4-bit quant + eval plan.
- SLOs: p95 <= 60ms for up to 256-token responses; tail latency for long sequences less critical but must not exceed 5s for 1024 tokens.
- Autoscaling: they want bounded vertical scaling rather than aggressive autoscaling (predictable billing). Suggest reserved pools + scheduled scaling windows.

Immediate gotchas / risks noted:
- A100 fp16 perf vs int8/4-bit: quantized kernels may need custom nvrtc kernel tuning; if we can't get parity they'll push for using fp16 and fewer replicas (cost/throughput trade-off).
- Co-lo power/cooling limits: operations mentioned a previous deploy that hit power budget during peak batch jobs — must recommend steady-state, avoid big batch windows.
- Network ACLs: their default inter-node firewall blocks multicast/broadcast and restricts ephemeral port ranges. Our runtime assumes some port openness for peer discovery; we need to validate port list.
- Telemetry: they will not permit traces containing prompt text. Our standard trace hooks will need sanitization or redaction.

Proposed short architecture (sketch):
- Private control plane (Redwood light control plane) inside their VPC via cross-account IAM role.
- Serving layer: 2x inference node pool: "low-latency" (sized for p95 work, small batch sizes, pinned cores/GPU affinity) and "throughput" pool (larger batch windows for embeddings/large requests).
- KV/prefix cache: optional local Redis cluster inside VPC; must support locking w/ TLS. Evaluate using our in-process prefix cache first to avoid extra ops.
- Secrets: integrate with AWS KMS + HSM adapter (Diego to ping security for integration checklist).
- Logging: no prompt storage; metrics only to CloudWatch -> Splunk ingest using forwarder.

Action items (owner / due):
- Maya: schedule infra deep-dive (45m) with Vela infra (S. Nwosu) — propose 2025-11-07 (DONE: invite sent).
- Liam: perf test plan for 4xA100 baseline + quantized 70B candidate (deliver by 2025-11-17).
- Priya: compliance checklist for PHI-adjacent data + log redaction doc (draft 2025-11-10).
- Diego: confirm HSM support matrix and sample HSM adapter docs (due 2025-11-14).
- Create JIRA epic and link PS tasks (assigned to me) -> JIRA-VP-4123 created (placeholder).

Quick perf notes to self:
- Start with a single-model shard per GPU and measure KV cache hit rate with typical chat prefixes (they expect lots of template prompts).
- Try enabling continuous batching with max latency 30ms to see throughput lift; but confirm it won't drive p95 above SLO.

Open questions (for Vela / internal):
- How strict is "no prompt persists" — is in-memory ephemeral acceptable if we never write to disk? Do they allow aggregated embeddings storage? (ASK legal)
- Can we use a small customer-accessible staging bucket for model weights, or do they require transfer via physical media for the air-gapped mode?
- What's their max acceptable per-month infra spend for pilot? They gave a vague "reasonable" number — need concrete cap to size pools.
- Who will own day-2 ops on their side? Named oncall person? (They mentioned S. Nwosu but need confirmation).

Notes to self / conversation fragments:
- "If we can't get 4-bit accuracy parity we pivot to fp16 and more nodes" — phrase from CTO, underline for later.
- Emphasize we can provide runtime knobs (batching, kv cache warmers, quant profiles) to hit different cost/latency targets.

Documentation/links to assemble for next call:
- Private deploy quickstart (internal): confluence:private-deploy-quickstart
- Quantization eval checklist: github:repo/quant-eval/checklist.md
- HSM adapter notes: internal doc (Diego to attach)

Next meeting agenda (prep checklist):
1) Validate infra constraints (ports, power, ssd mapping) — infra deep-dive.
2) Share perf test plan and sync on metrics we'll collect for go/no-go.
3) Review compliance redaction plan (Priya).
4) Decide on pilot budget cap and node sizing.

Tone / internal guidance: keep early conversations low-friction — propose 2 pilot configs (cost-optimised + low-latency) and let them pick. Avoid promising air-gap fully until we confirm HSM/physical transfer plan.

End of scratchpad. Will convert into a tidy follow-up email + JIRA tickets after infra deep-dive.

-- Maya
